text: {"lesson":{"schemaVersion":1,"title":"Lesson 41: Shared Stories, Shared Lessons: Seminar and Podcast Showcase","lessonType":"writing","header":{"focusStandards":["SL.6.1","SL.6.2","SL.6.4","SL.6.5","SL.6.6"],"supportingStandards":["SL.6.1.a","SL.6.1.b","SL.6.1.c","SL.6.1.d","SL.6.2","SL.6.4","SL.6.4.a","SL.6.5","SL.6.6"],"eldStandards":["ELD.PI.6.1","ELD.PI.6.4","ELD.PII.6.6"],"mediaLiteracyStandards":["MSLS.6.4.3.a"],"objectives":[{"kind":"content","text":"Students will present the key claim and evidence from their explanatory essays orally in a seminar or podcast, listen actively, paraphrase peers, and connect ideas from The Lightning Thief to modern values."},{"kind":"content","text":"Students will submit final essay drafts and self-reflect on both their written and oral performance."},{"kind":"language","text":"Students will use formal, complete sentences, transitions, and complex sentences with because and although to cite evidence and respond to peers, and will adapt their speech for a formal presentation."},{"kind":"foundational-skills","text":"Students will rehearse clear pronunciation of myth names and academic vocabulary, and practice paraphrasing a peer before responding."}],"essentialQuestions":["What shared lessons do ancient myths and modern stories teach, and why do those lessons still matter today?","How can we use evidence and careful listening to share and build ideas with others?"],"connections":{"knowledgeBuilding":"Students have read The Lightning Thief and studied how Riordan adapts Greek myths. Today they speak from the evidence in their essays to show what they learned.","enduringUnderstanding":"Stories carry values across time. Speaking with evidence and listening with care help us understand those shared lessons and the people who share them.","futureLessons":"Students who need more time to finish or present the Performance Task will use the next Flex Day (F5) to catch up. Their self-reflection will guide what they work on next.","performanceTask":"This is the delivery step of Shared Stories, Shared Lessons. Students submit final essays, present orally with evidence and a visual or audio element, and complete the Self-Reflection graphic organizer."},"vocabulary":[{"word":"paraphrase","definition":"to restate someone else's idea in your own words while keeping the meaning","tier":"support"},{"word":"seminar","definition":"a small-group discussion in which everyone prepares, shares ideas, and responds to each other","tier":"support"},{"word":"podcast","definition":"a recorded audio conversation or talk that an audience can listen to","tier":"support"},{"word":"modern values","definition":"beliefs about what is important today, such as honesty, loyalty, courage, and fairness","tier":"support"},{"word":"transition","definition":"a word or phrase that connects ideas and shows how they relate, such as for example, because, or however","tier":"support"},{"word":"self-reflection","definition":"thinking carefully about your own work to name strengths and next steps","tier":"support"}],"texts":[{"title":"The Lightning Thief","author":"Rick Riordan"},{"title":"Students' final explanatory essays (Performance Task)","author":"Students"}]},"sections":[{"kind":"launch","title":"Launch","purpose":"Energize students for the showcase, name the success criteria for speaking and listening, and set the roles for the seminar or podcast.","activities":[{"id":"launch-showcase-norms","title":"Showcase Norms and Goals","minutes":5,"standards":["SL.6.1"],"routine":"Turn and Talk","blocks":[{"type":"paragraph","audience":"teacher","text":"Today is a celebration of learning. Keep this Launch brisk. Post the four seminar roles (Speaker, Paraphraser, Questioner, Timekeeper) and the success criteria where all students can see them. Decide before class whether groups will talk face to face (seminar) or record audio (podcast). The routine is the same either way."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"For several lessons you have written about what Percy's story and the Greek myths teach us. Today you get to share those ideas out loud and hear what your classmates learned."},{"type":"directions","text":"Read the success criteria on the board: (1) Speak about your claim and evidence in a clear order. (2) Use a strong voice, eye contact, and clear pronunciation. (3) Paraphrase a classmate before you respond. (4) Connect at least one idea to a modern value. Then turn to a partner and talk about the question below."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which of these four goals will be hardest for you today, and what is one thing you can do to meet it?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Paraphrasing will be hardest for me because I usually just say my own idea. I can listen for the main point and start with, 'So you're saying...'"},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Good. Hold onto that goal. You will check it at the end of class."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"tip","text":"Name the group roles quickly and let groups choose who starts as Timekeeper. The roles rotate each round, so no one needs to be perfect on the first try."}]}]},{"kind":"literacy-lab","title":"Literacy Lab","purpose":"Build the two foundational habits students need for a strong showcase: clear pronunciation of myth names and academic vocabulary, and paraphrasing a peer in a complete sentence before responding.","activities":[{"id":"lab-pronounce-names","title":"Say It Clearly: Myth Names and Academic Words","minutes":4,"standards":["SL.6.4","SL.6.6"],"routine":"Choral Rehearsal","blocks":[{"type":"paragraph","audience":"teacher","text":"Display these names and words with syllable breaks: Poseidon (puh-SY-dun), Athena (uh-THEE-nuh), Hades (HAY-deez), Medusa (muh-DOO-suh), Persephone (per-SEF-uh-nee), Chiron (KY-ron), Olympus (oh-LIM-pus), evidence (EV-ih-dunts), paraphrase (PAIR-uh-fraze), perspective (per-SPEK-tiv)."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"teach","text":"A presenter who says names clearly sounds prepared, and listeners can follow the ideas. I say each word, you repeat it, then you say it once more to a partner."},{"type":"directions","text":"Repeat each word after your teacher. Then choose two words you will use in your presentation. Say each one to a partner in a full sentence, such as: 'In The Lightning Thief, Poseidon is Percy's father.'"},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which word do you want to practice one more time before you present?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Persephone, because I always rush it. I'm going to say it slowly: per-SEF-uh-nee."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"note","text":"Listen for stress on the right syllable, not perfection. Praise effort and model again without calling out a mistake in front of the class."}]},{"id":"lab-paraphrase-routine","title":"Paraphrase Before You Respond","minutes":6,"standards":["SL.6.1","SL.6.1.d","SL.6.6"],"routine":"Paraphrase Passport","blocks":[{"type":"teacher-script","move":"teach","text":"In a good seminar, you show you listened before you add your own thinking. First, paraphrase: say the speaker's idea in your own words. Then respond: add evidence, a question, or a connection. Use a complete sentence each time."},{"type":"paragraph","audience":"shared","text":"Paraphrase: 'So you are saying that ___ because ___.' Respond: 'I agree/see it a little differently because, in the text, ___.' Connect: 'This idea matters today because ___.'"},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Listen to my example. A student says, 'Percy shows loyalty because he goes to the Underworld to save his mom.' I paraphrase: 'So you are saying that Percy's loyalty is proven by his risk to rescue his mother.' Then I respond: 'I agree, and I also noticed he stays loyal to Grover, which shows loyalty can mean friends too.'"},{"type":"directions","text":"With a partner, take turns. Partner A states one claim from their essay in one sentence. Partner B paraphrases using the frame, then responds. Switch roles."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"What did your partner do that made you feel heard?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"My partner said my idea back in her own words and got it right. Then she added a different example from the book, so I knew she was really listening."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Students practice paraphrasing and complete-sentence responses to exchange ideas with a partner and adapt language for an academic purpose.","sayAsk":"Model the frame twice, slowly. Say: 'So you are saying that Percy is brave because he faces Medusa.' Ask: 'What did your partner say? Say it in your words.' Frames: So you are saying that ___. I agree because ___. Another way to see it is ___. Emerging students can use 'You say ___. I think ___.' Allow quiet rehearsal with a partner before sharing.","watchFor":"If students repeat the speaker word for word, then prompt: 'Change two words but keep the same meaning.' If students skip the paraphrase and jump to their own idea, then say: 'Start with So you are saying.' Success: Student restates a partner's idea accurately in a complete sentence and adds a related comment."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: Paraphrasing accurately","tryThis":"Have students jot three key words while listening, then build the paraphrase from those words. Let them ask, 'Did I get that right?' to check."},{"situation":"Ready for extension","tryThis":"Ask students to paraphrase two speakers at once and show how the ideas connect, using 'Both of you suggest ___, but ___ adds ___.'"}]}]}]},{"kind":"learning-in-action","title":"Learning in Action","purpose":"Students submit final essays, present their claim and evidence orally with a visual or audio element, listen and respond in small-group seminars or podcast recordings, and connect the lessons of The Lightning Thief to modern values.","activities":[{"id":"lia-prepare-submit","title":"Prepare Your Presentation and Submit Your Essay","minutes":6,"standards":["SL.6.4","SL.6.4.a","SL.6.5","SL.6.1.a"],"routine":"Rehearse and Submit","blocks":[{"type":"text-reference","title":"Students' final explanatory essays (Performance Task)"},{"type":"text-reference","title":"The Lightning Thief"},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"teach","text":"You will give a two-minute talk from your essay. Do not read it word for word. Open with your main claim. Give your strongest piece of evidence from The Lightning Thief. Explain how it supports your claim. Close with the modern value your idea connects to. Use transitions like 'first,' 'for example,' and 'as a result' so listeners can follow."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Choose one visual or sound that clarifies your point: a picture of a character, a symbol, a short chart, or a sound or music cue for a podcast. It should help your listener understand, not just decorate."},{"type":"directions","text":"1. Submit your final essay draft. 2. Mark your claim, one piece of evidence, and your modern value on your essay or notes card. 3. Choose your visual or audio element. 4. Rehearse your two-minute talk once quietly, practicing your voice, eye contact, and myth names."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which sentence from your essay will open your talk, and why will it grab your listeners?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"I'll open with 'Percy's loyalty to his friends matters as much today as it did in myths.' It tells my claim right away and makes people think about their own friends."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"tip","text":"Collect final essays as students begin rehearsing. A rehearsal card with three bullets (claim, evidence, value) works better than a full script. Circulate and listen for a clear order of ideas."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Students plan and rehearse a formal presentation, adjusting language choices for an academic audience and purpose.","sayAsk":"Say: 'Today we speak like presenters, not like we are texting.' Model one casual and one formal version: 'Percy is super loyal' versus 'Percy demonstrates loyalty when he risks his life to rescue his mother.' Frames: My claim is ___. One example from the text is ___. This shows ___ because ___. This connects to the modern value of ___. Allow students to rehearse in a home language first and then say it in English.","watchFor":"If students read their essay aloud word for word, then prompt: 'Look at your three bullets and say it to me in your own words.' If students use slang or incomplete sentences, then say: 'Say that again as a formal sentence.' Success: Student states a claim, evidence, and value in a logical order using formal sentences."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: Organizing a two-minute talk","tryThis":"Give a three-box card: Claim, Evidence, Why it matters today. Let students rehearse by pointing to each box as they speak."},{"situation":"Ready for extension","tryThis":"Invite students to add a counterpoint using 'Although some might say ___, the text shows ___,' and to use a question to engage listeners."}]}]},{"id":"lia-seminar-podcast","title":"Seminar or Podcast Rounds","minutes":18,"standards":["SL.6.1","SL.6.1.a","SL.6.1.b","SL.6.1.c","SL.6.1.d","SL.6.4","SL.6.4.a","SL.6.5","SL.6.6","MSLS.6.4.3.a"],"routine":"Small-Group Seminar / Podcast","blocks":[{"type":"paragraph","audience":"teacher","text":"Form groups of four. Each round is about four minutes: the Speaker presents for about two minutes, the Paraphraser restates the main idea, the Questioner asks one specific follow-up, and the group responds for the remaining time. The Timekeeper keeps the pace. Rotate roles after each round. If recording a podcast, use one device per group; the Speaker begins by introducing themselves and the episode title, such as 'Shared Stories, Shared Lessons: Loyalty.'"},{"type":"directions","text":"Follow the round: 1. Speaker presents the claim, evidence, and modern value, showing a visual or playing a sound cue. 2. Paraphraser says, 'So you are saying that ___.' 3. Questioner asks one question that needs evidence or explanation. 4. Speaker answers; group members add connections to modern values. 5. Rotate roles."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Remember your engagement tools. Change your voice to stress important words, use a gesture to show a key idea, and ask your listeners a question. Keep your eyes up, speak loudly enough for the last person in your group, and use clear pronunciation."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"As a listener, what question could you ask that pushes a speaker to explain their evidence more?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"I could ask, 'How does that quote show Percy is loyal and not just scared?' or 'Where in the book did you find that detail?'"},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"After a speaker finishes, how can you connect their idea to a modern value?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"I can say, 'This connects to honesty today because people still have to decide whether to tell the truth when it's hard, like Percy does.'"},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"note","text":"Circulate with a checklist: clear order of ideas, evidence cited, volume and eye contact, paraphrase before response, formal speech. Do not interrupt a speaker. Note strengths to share during Look Back. If time runs short, shorten the last round so that every student speaks."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Students exchange ideas in small groups, following turn-taking rules, asking questions, paraphrasing, and combining ideas in complex sentences to show reasons and contrasts.","sayAsk":"Say: 'Use because to give a reason and although to show a different side.' Model: 'Percy shows courage because he faces danger for others.' 'Although Percy is afraid, he keeps going.' Frames: I agree with ___ because ___. Although ___, I think ___. Can you give an example from the text? This matters today because ___. Emerging students may respond with 'I agree because ___' or a yes-no question; Bridging students should add evidence and build on a peer.","watchFor":"If a student is silent, then offer a sentence frame and wait time, or have them respond to a peer's question after a partner rehearsal. If a student answers in single words, then prompt: 'Say that in a full sentence with because.' Success: Student asks or answers at least one question, paraphrases a peer, and uses because or although to connect ideas."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: Speaking in front of peers","tryThis":"Let the student present first to a partner, then to the group, or record the talk as a podcast. Provide the three-box card and allow reading the claim sentence aloud."},{"situation":"Struggling with: Asking a specific question","tryThis":"Give question starters: 'What evidence shows ___?' 'How does ___ connect to ___?' 'Why does that matter today?'"},{"situation":"Ready for extension","tryThis":"Assign the student to synthesize the round: 'Three of us noticed ___, but ___ added a different perspective on ___.' Ask for a follow-up question that compares two myths or stories."}]}]},{"id":"lia-listening-notes-synthesis","title":"What We Learned: Values Across Voices","minutes":6,"standards":["SL.6.2","SL.6.1.d","SL.6.1","SL.6.6"],"routine":"Think-Pair-Share","blocks":[{"type":"directions","text":"Look at your listening notes and think about the talks, visuals, and sounds you heard. Write one sentence that explains how a classmate's evidence or visual helped you understand a lesson from The Lightning Thief. Then share with a partner from a different group."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Information comes through voices, pictures, and sounds. Today you took in ideas in all three ways. Now explain what they added to our shared understanding of the unit's topic."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"What did a classmate's talk, visual, or sound add to your understanding of a shared lesson from Percy's story?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"A classmate showed a picture of Percy and Grover back to back, and it made me see that loyalty means being brave for someone else. I had only thought about loyalty to family before."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which modern values did several of you name, and why do these stories still teach them?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Many of us talked about courage, loyalty, and fairness. These stories still teach them because people today face tough choices and need to decide what kind of person to be, just like Percy does."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Students explain how information presented orally and visually contributes to understanding, using complex sentences to connect ideas.","sayAsk":"Say: 'Tell your partner what you learned and why.' Frames: My classmate's ___ helped me understand ___ because ___. Although I first thought ___, I now think ___. A value we share is ___. Emerging students can say 'The picture shows ___.' Expanding and Bridging students should add because or although.","watchFor":"If students only describe the visual, then prompt: 'What did it help you understand about the story?' If students state a value without evidence, then ask: 'Which part of a talk showed that?' Success: Student explains how a peer's evidence, visual, or sound contributed to understanding a lesson."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: Explaining how media contributed","tryThis":"Provide the frame 'The ___ helped me understand ___ because ___.' Let students point to the part of their notes first."},{"situation":"Ready for extension","tryThis":"Ask students to compare how a spoken explanation and a visual showed the same value, and which was more effective for the audience and why."}]}]}]},{"kind":"look-back","title":"Look Back","purpose":"Students reflect on their written and oral performance and begin the Self-Reflection graphic organizer.","activities":[{"id":"lookback-self-reflection","title":"Begin the Self-Reflection","minutes":5,"standards":["SL.6.1","SL.6.4","SL.6.6"],"routine":"Quick Write","blocks":[{"type":"directions","text":"Begin your Self-Reflection graphic organizer. Write a response to the question below. Include one strength in your essay, one strength in your speaking or listening, and one next step."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"How did your written essay and your spoken presentation work together, and what is one thing you will do differently next time?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"My essay gave me strong evidence, so I felt confident when I talked. I also paraphrased my group members, which helped me listen better. Next time I will look up more so I'm not reading from my card."},{"type":"paragraph","audience":"shared","text":"Optional sentence starters: My strongest skill was ___. Next time I will ___."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"tip","text":"Share two or three strengths you noticed during rounds, such as a clear transition, a strong paraphrase, or a creative visual. Collect or check that students have started the organizer."}]}]},{"kind":"homework","title":"Homework","purpose":"Students finish the reflection that closes the Performance Task.","activities":[{"id":"homework-finish-reflection","title":"Finish Self-Reflection","minutes":0,"standards":["SL.6.4"],"routine":"Independent Reflection","blocks":[{"type":"directions","text":"Finish the Self-Reflection graphic organizer. Be specific about your essay, your presentation, and your listening. Bring it to class."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"note","text":"Optional. Students who have not yet presented or submitted their essay can use the next Flex Day (F5)."}]}]}]},"digest":{"summary":"Students submit final essays and present their claims, evidence, and modern-value connections in small-group seminars or podcast recordings, practicing paraphrasing and formal speech. They close by starting the Self-Reflection organizer on their written and oral work.","keyActivities":["Showcase norms and goals Turn and Talk","Pronunciation of myth names and academic vocabulary","Paraphrase Before You Respond routine","Prepare presentation and submit final essay","Seminar or podcast rounds with rotating roles","Think-Pair-Share synthesis of values across voices","Quick Write self-reflection"],"vocabularyTaught":["paraphrase","seminar","podcast","modern values","transition","self-reflection"],"standardsCovered":["SL.6.1","SL.6.2","SL.6.4","SL.6.5","SL.6.6","SL.6.1.a","SL.6.1.b","SL.6.1.c","SL.6.1.d","SL.6.4.a","MSLS.6.4.3.a","ELD.PI.6.1","ELD.PI.6.4","ELD.PII.6.6"]}}
